`AutoNEB` reads `prefix000.traj` and `prefix001.traj` and grows the band with `autoneb_run`. The constructor arguments match `ase.mep.AutoNEB`. The steps are the band's FIRE solver. `maxstep` is read from the optimizer class signature when that parameter has a default. `smooth_curve=True`, a non-FIRE optimizer, and `method` `spline` or `string` raise `UnsupportedFeature`. The final images are written back to `prefixNNN.traj`. Per-iteration trajectory files are not written. The initial fill matches ASE when `n_simul` is 1 or 3.

## From ASE's dimer and from Sella
`rgsaddle.ase.MinModeAtoms(atoms, control=None, eigenmodes=None, *, mode=..., method='lbfgs')` estimates a dimer or Lanczos mode and returns the effective force. A `DimerControl` carries ASE's parameter names, one copy per instance. `eigenmode_method`, `dimer_separation`, `max_num_rot`, `f_rot_min`, and `maximum_translation` are the kind, the finite-difference length, the rotation cap, the rotation residual, and the per-atom step cap. `order` other than 1, a displacement mask, extrapolated forces, and `use_central_forces=False` raise `UnsupportedFeature`. A knob this step does not read raises `UnsupportedFeature` when it is not the default, so a changed `trial_angle` or `f_rot_max` is not a silent no-op. Above the well the perpendicular force is dropped. Below it the force along the mode is reflected. `MinModeTranslate(dimeratoms, logfile='-', trajectory=None)` is an ASE `Optimizer` subclass whose first argument is the `MinModeAtoms`: each step is one Rust minimum-mode translation, and a `DimerControl` also requires a negative curvature. The translation is the core's L-BFGS step unless `MinModeAtoms` is built with `method='fire'`; it is not ASE's Newton line search. An ASE optimizer can drive `MinModeAtoms` directly as well.

`rgsaddle.ase.Sella(atoms, order=1)` is the saddle optimizer. `run(fmax, steps)` is ASE's loop. One step is the partitioned rational-function trust step, not a dimer translation. Masses come from `atoms.get_masses`.

## From eOn
The band tangents, springs, projections, and the climbing-image arm follow eOn's branch structure. `CiConfig::after(0.5)` is eOn's `ci_after`. `after_rel` is `ci_after_rel`. `always` climbs from the first evaluation. The minimum-mode dimer is eOn's improved dimer: `rotation_angle_tol` defaults to five degrees (`converged_angle`), and a rotation stops when the trial or the fitted angle falls under it, on `rotation_tol`, or at `max_rotations`. It does not infer the classic torque window; `rotation_angle_tol` 0 restores that window at the stock residual, and `set_torque_window(Some(true))` adds it to the improved dimer. Lanczos stops on the window at two vectors. eOn's Lanczos stops on the relative change of its lowest Ritz value (`lanczos_tolerance`), which `set_lanczos_rel_tol` sets here without the window.

eOn's client reads a config file and a potential plugin. Here the host passes positions and a surface. There is no system name, species table, or potential key in the session. A solid-state band takes one cell per image and the Cauchy stress through `BandSurface::eval_cells`.

Live Onsager-Machlup displacements are the atomic force over `2k`. A solid-state band has a cell block in the same vector, so that spring is refused at construction rather than applied as zeros.

# Step a point stencil (`docs/orgmode/howto/stencil.org`)

> Unified point stencil builder across Rust, C, C++, and Python

`Stencil::point` builds a minimiser, a dimer, Lanczos, ART, or eigen following. The defaults match `MinModeConfig`: forward difference, `dr ` 1e-3=, rotation tolerance `1e-4`, rotation angle five degrees (zero disables it), 20 rotations, Krylov dimension 12, FIRE with opening timestep 1.0, and maximum move 0.2. When the per-atom cap shortens a negative-curvature FIRE step and the arrival is no longer negative, that step is replaced from the last negative point by 0.01 times the reflected force. Dimer and Lanczos are a `MinModeSession`. Dimer rotational conjugate-gradient history crosses translations. A negative curvature reflects the parallel force. A curvature that is not negative moves the largest atom by the maximum move along the mode and drops the perpendicular force; within half that step of the minimum along the mode it keeps the mode's orientation, for eigen following as well. Henkelman and Jónsson (1999), doi:10.1063/1.480097. Goswami, Gunde, and Jónsson, Front. Chem. (2026), doi:10.3389/fchem.2026.1807063, Eq. 9.

```rust
let mut search = Stencil::point(x0)
    .preset(Preset::Dimer)
    .mode(seed)
    .build()?;
let report = search.step(&surface)?;
```

ART pushes along the seed until the curvature falls under `art_threshold` (default 0), then climbs with Lanczos. Malek and Mousseau (2000), doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.62.7723. Eigen following builds a central-difference Hessian, calls `exact_eigh`, and makes the largest-magnitude component of the lowest mode positive. `build` rejects `Climb::Reflect` on a minimiser, a window on a point, a zero thread count, and ART without a mode solver.

`Stencil::band` checks the array and then returns `band presets stay on feat/band-methods-zoom`. Zoom, energy-weighted springs, and the band side of the builder are that branch. The chain, the mesh (remesh, insert, window), and the point controller are on this branch.

From C, `rgsaddle_stencil_config_new` takes the preset discriminant. Unknown keys return `RGSADDLE_INVALID_PARAMETER`. `rgsaddle_last_error` is thread-local. `rgsaddle_stencil_run` loops over `rgsaddle_stencil_step`. The report opens with `struct_size`. The older band and min-mode entries stay step-only, and the ABI minor stays 16.

From Python, `rgsaddle.Stencil.point(x, preset`"dimer")= takes a C-contiguous float64 vector. `step(surface)` releases the thread, and the surface callback re-attaches. `rgsaddle.ase.Point(atoms, preset`"dimer").run(fmax, steps)= is an ASE `Optimizer` whose `step` is one stencil step. A second thread that enters the same handle raises `RuntimeError`.

`Chain::evaluate` writes each image from a block of one. Threads 1, 2, 3, and 8 produce the same bytes. A point preset is one row, so its thread count does not change the bytes either.

# Formal stencil (`docs/orgmode/howto/formal.org`)

> Lean 4 formal proofs and MPFR differential verification

The climbing image with a zero doubly-nudged term is the Householder reflection of the true force. Goswami, Gunde, and Jónsson, Front. Chem. (2026), doi:10.3389/fchem.2026.1807063, Eq. 9, is the identity used first. The same reflection is the negative-curvature dimer translation. Henkelman and Jónsson, J. Chem. Phys. 111, 7010 (1999), doi:10.1063/1.480097, define that step. The improved tangent is Henkelman and Jónsson, J. Chem. Phys. 113, 9978 (2000), doi:10.1063/1.1323224.

## Check
```console
$ cd formal && ./check.sh
$ (cd formal && lake exe mirror)
$ cargo test --features capi --test formal_mirror
```

`formal/check.sh` builds the pinned Lean toolchain and refuses `sorry`, `admit`, and axioms beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. `lake exe mirror` writes `formal/golden/stencil.json`. The Rust test compares those bits.

The MPFR comparison is a separate feature so a default build does not link GMP.

```console
$ cargo test --features capi,verify --lib differential -- --nocapture
```

That test asserts only the dot-product bound in Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., SIAM, 2002, doi:10.1137/1.9780898718027, Section 3.1. It prints the largest ULP it saw.

The two-dimensional reflected Hessian `diag(-a, b)` has eigenvalues of positive real part exactly when the mode's first component exceeds `1/sqrt(2)`. The same threshold in dimension 3 and higher is open. `validation/stencil/fortyfive.py` records the search.

# Mass-weighted reaction paths (`docs/orgmode/explanation/mep.org`)

> Mass-weighted intrinsic reaction coordinates and unweighted minimum energy paths

An intrinsic reaction coordinate follows the gradient in mass-weighted coordinates. With `x_mw = sqrt(m) x`, its tangent is the normalized negative mass-weighted gradient.

The inner steps of both sphere kinds use a moving constraint whose radius is measured in that metric. The displacement and the stored path offset appear together in the constraint, so the sphere is not the unit sphere centred at the coordinate origin. The steps follow the full mass-weighted gradient. Only the launch mode that `from_surface` estimates leaves out the excluded directions of the surface, such as rigid-body motion.

The launch direction is the lowest eigenvector `u` of the mass-weighted Hessian `M^{-1/2} H M^{-1/2}`, taken as the Cartesian displacement `M^{-1/2} u`. A surface that supports Hessian actions can supply it without materializing a dense Hessian. An existing dense Hessian can use the corresponding eigensolver. The host chooses the method and verifies the physical saddle before tracing its branches.

In unweighted Cartesian coordinates, a minimum energy path between two basins satisfies \(\nabla V(x)^\perp = 0\) along the curve. `BandSession` approximates that path either by the nudged elastic band, which projects the potential force perpendicular to a discrete tangent and spaces images with tangential springs, or by the simplified string method of E, Ren, and Vanden-Eijnden, J. Chem. Phys. 126, 164103 (2007), doi:10.1063/1.2720838 [eSimplifiedImprovedString2007] (`StringConfig`), which evolves images under the full potential force \(-\nabla V\) and restores equal arc length geometrically on the not-a-knot cubic spline or the polyline after each step.

# One stencil (`docs/orgmode/explanation/one-stencil.org`)

> Householder reflection shared by climbing-image NEB and minimum-mode searches

The dimer translation and the climbing image are one Householder reflection of the true force. Goswami, Gunde, and Jónsson, Front. Chem. (2026), doi:10.3389/fchem.2026.1807063, Eqs. 3, 8, and 9, and Sec. 2.3.1 and Sec. 4. The dimer is that reflection on a three-image chain with free ends. Goswami (2026), arXiv:2603.10992, doi:10.48550/arXiv.2603.10992, Eqs. 2.14-2.16.

A preset chooses the sides, the tangent, the coupling, the climb, and the mesh. `Stencil::point` runs a minimiser, the dimer, Lanczos, ART, and eigen following. Dimer and Lanczos construct `MinModeSession`, so the recorded position and energy hashes stay the same. `Stencil::band` names the band presets and returns the `feat/band-methods-zoom` seam. Zoom, the recomputed energy-weighted spring, and the band keys are that branch.

| Preset | Tangent | Climb | Mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| minimiser | none | none | none |
| dimer | axis | reflect if the curvature is negative, otherwise ascend | rotation |
| Lanczos | Ritz | as the dimer | Lanczos |
| ART | seed, then Ritz | ascend until the curvature drops, then reflect | Lanczos |
| eigen following | lowest eigenvector | as the dimer | dense central-difference `exact_eigh` |

rgmin started as Rohit Goswami's xtsci-optimize (2023-2024), which composed minimisers from small strategy objects. The stencil core extends that to saddle and band methods. eOn v2.9.0.1 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.18529496. Goswami (2025), arXiv:2510.21368, doi:10.48550/arXiv.2510.21368.

`Chain::evaluate` owns one block per image. The block size is fixed at one image and does not depend on the thread count. Each block is written back by index after the surface call. Remesh, insert, and window do not call the surface. Image ids survive an insert.

The C surface is `rgsaddle_stencil_*` with an opaque config, typed key setters, and a thread-local `rgsaddle_last_error`. `include/rgsaddle/stencil.hpp` is the RAII wrapper. Python `rgsaddle.Stencil.point` and `rgsaddle.ase.Point` call that wrapper. `Point.run` uses an ASE `Optimizer` subclass. The extension is nanobind with `Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED` on a free-threaded build.

Method papers, after the citations above: Henkelman and Jónsson (1999), doi:10.1063/1.480097; Henkelman, Uberuaga, and Jónsson (2000), doi:10.1063/1.1329672; Henkelman and Jónsson (2000), doi:10.1063/1.1323224; Jónsson, Mills, and Jacobsen (1998); Ásgeirsson et al. (2021), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.1c00462; Kolsbjerg, Groves, and Hammer (2016), doi:10.1063/1.4961868; Malek and Mousseau (2000), doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.62.7723; Smidstrup et al. (2014), doi:10.1063/1.4878664; Schmerwitz, Ásgeirsson, and Jónsson (2024), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.3c01111; Curtis, Powell, and Reid (1974), doi:10.1093/imamat/13.1.117.

A benchmark that changes iterates cites Goswami, AIP Adv. (2025), doi:10.1063/5.0283639, first. This branch does not change the recorded iterates.

# Hyperplane methods on one geometric footing (`docs/orgmode/explanation/hyperplane-methods.org`)

> PAFI, OH-TST, and constrained-ensemble samplers on one geometric footing

## Scope and provenance

The implementation starts from the operator construction used by Goswami,
Gunde, and Jónsson, /Enhanced climbing image nudged elastic band method with
Hessian eigenmode alignment/, /Frontiers in Chemistry/ 14 (2026),
doi:10.3389/fchem.2026.1807063: dimer translation and climbing-image
translation are reflections made from the same rank-one projector.  Goswami,
/A Tutorial Review of Bayesian Optimization with Gaussian Processes to
Accelerate Stationary Point Searches/ (2026), arXiv:2603.10992, writes the
dimer construction in the same form.  The cost accounting used when these
operators are compared follows Goswami, /Bayesian hierarchical models for
quantitative estimates for performance metrics applied to saddle search
algorithms/, /AIP Advances/ 15 (2025), doi:10.1063/5.0283639.  These papers
are cited first because they are the direct provenance of the implementation
and its comparisons; they did not introduce PAFI or OH-TST.

The method sources are:

- Swinburne and Marinica, /Unsupervised Calculation of Free Energy Barriers
  in Large Crystalline Systems/, /Physical Review Letters/ 120, 135503
  (2018), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.135503 (PAFI).
- Jóhannesson and Jónsson, /Optimization of hyperplanar transition states/,
  /The Journal of Chemical Physics/ 115, 9644-9656 (2001),
  doi:10.1063/1.1415499 (OH-TST).
- Bligaard and Jónsson, /Optimization of hyperplanar transition states:
  Application to 2D test problems/, /Computer Physics Communications/ 169,
  284-288 (2005), doi:10.1016/j.cpc.2005.03.064 (the twisted-path
  validation).
- Hermes, Sargsyan, Najm, and Zádor, /Sella, an Open-Source
  Automation-Friendly Molecular Saddle Point Optimizer/, /Journal of Chemical
  Theory and Computation/ 18, 6974-6988 (2022),
  doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.2c00395.
- Absil, Mahony, and Sepulchre, /Optimization Algorithms on Matrix
  Manifolds/, Princeton University Press (2008),
  doi:10.1515/9781400830244.

## Symmetry-unique hard regions and rate multiplicity

A dividing hyperplane is infinite.  In a crystal it can therefore intersect
several symmetry-equivalent images of the same transition.  Sampling all of
them is wasteful and can mix images.  `SymmetryUniqueRegion` instead builds
the Voronoi cell of one representative configuration under point- or
space-group operations that leave the plane invariant.  Its faces are hard
half-spaces.  MD reflects the in-plane velocity normal to a crossed face;
GHMC rejects an outside proposal.  There is no collective variable, spring,
window, or soft wall.

The region reports the number of distinct in-plane images as its
`degeneracy`.  `RateMultiplicity` keeps that number separate from the number
of paths or hop directions:

\[
k_{\rm total}=m_{\rm path}m_{\rm plane}k_{\rm unique}.
\]

Each symmetry orbit belongs in exactly one factor.  The twelve fcc
nearest-neighbour vacancy-hop directions are =m_path=12.  They are not the
degeneracy of one hop's dividing plane.  That factor is the order of the
subgroup that fixes both the reactant and the chosen saddle, the in-plane
symmetry of that plane.  Jóhannesson and Jónsson, Secs. II D and III D,
sample one such part of the hyperplane; the construction is in
[crystal operations and symmetry-unique regions](explanation/symmetry-regions.html).
Putting the twelve directions into `m_plane` as well as `m_path` counts each
hop twice.

`AffineSymmetry` and `SymmetrySource` accept generic configuration-space
point- or space-group maps.  `PeriodicSymmetryOperations` evaluates their
per-atom displacements with `minimage::Cell`.  `readcon-core` currently
supplies structures and cells but no generic symmetry-operation source, while
`minimage` supplies periodic geometry but no space-group finder.  Automatic
discovery therefore belongs as a future patch to one of those owning
libraries; rgsaddle consumes operations supplied by the host and does not
duplicate crystallographic symmetry discovery.

`RegionIntersection` composes the primary symmetry cell with `PathSlab`
(between neighbouring path planes) and `QuenchedTransitionRegion` (outside
either rgmin-quenched basin).  It rejects more than one non-unit degeneracy,
preventing accidental multiplication of overlapping symmetry counts.
Predicate faces without a geometric penetration depth return to the last
contained point before velocity reflection.

The engine-neutral sampling budget carries the same region.  The analytic
BAOAB/GHMC implementation consumes it through its existing drift or proposal
step.  LAMMPS hard-region sampling is pending a lammpc capability that applies
a host boundary callback after every `lammpc_session_md_step`, restores a
complete accepted state on rejection, and refreshes forces after reflection.
The callback registration entry points already exist, but current lammpc main
does not apply them to constrained MD steps.  Until lammpc advertises that
behavior, the LAMMPS adapter fails closed when a sampling budget carries a
region.

## One constraint and its metric

Let Cartesian coordinates be \(x\), let \(M\) be a positive diagonal mass
matrix, and put

\[
q=M^{1/2}x .
\]

A Cartesian plane with covector \(a\) through \(x_0\) is
\(a^{T}(x-x_0)=0\).  In mass-weighted coordinates it has unit normal

\[
\nu={M^{-1/2}a\over\sqrt{a^{T}M^{-1}a}},\qquad q_0=M^{1/2}x_0 .
\]

Its tangent space and Euclidean projector in \(q\) are

\[
T_q{\cal H}=\{v:\nu^Tv=0\},\qquad
P_q=I-\nu\nu^T .
\]

Mapping a tangent displacement back to Cartesian coordinates gives

\[
P_x=M^{-1/2}P_qM^{1/2}
   =I-{M^{-1}aa^T\over a^TM^{-1}a}.
\]

Forces are covectors, so their Cartesian map is \(P_x^T\), not \(P_x\).
The code therefore performs all OH-TST geometry in \(q\).  PAFI without
explicit masses is the unit-mass case.  `MassWeighted` and
`Hyperplane::from_cartesian` perform the two coordinate maps rather than
hiding a metric in a dot product.

The affine level set is a flat embedded manifold.  Its retraction is exact:

\[
R_q(v)=q+P_qv,\qquad
\Pi_{\cal H}(y)=y-\nu\nu^T(y-q_0).
\]

For a non-unit normal \(n\), both occurrences of \(\nu\nu^T\) become
\(nn^T/(n^Tn)\).  This is the arithmetic retained by PAFI.

## PAFI: a fixed family of planes

Let \(X(s)\) be a path parameterised by arc length, \(n(s)=X'(s)\), and
\(n'(s)=X''(s)\).  PAFI samples the canonical distribution restricted to

\[
{\cal H}_s=\{q:(q-X(s))^Tn(s)=0\}.
\]

Projected Brownian dynamics removes the normal part of drift and noise with
\(P_s=I-nn^T\), then applies the exact affine restoration.  With

\[
\psi(q,s)=(q-X(s))^Tn'(s),
\]

the mean-force estimator used in `pafi.rs` is

\[
{dF\over ds}
 =\left\langle
   \bigl(\nabla V(q)^Tn(s)\bigr)\bigl(1-\psi(q,s)\bigr)
  \right\rangle_{{\cal H}_s}.
\]

`average_hyperplane` estimates this expression and its block error.
`pafi_profile` evaluates independent fixed planes along the path.
`integrate_profile` applies the trapezoid rule and propagates the plane
errors.  PAFI optimises neither \(X\) nor a plane normal; path quality and
sampling error are separate inputs to the result.

## OH-TST: optimise the dividing plane

Write a plane using a pivot \(c\), unit normal \(\nu\), and offset \(d\):

\[
{\cal H}(\nu,d;c)=\{q:\nu^T(q-c)=d\}.
\]

Its configurational free energy, up to the common normalisation, is

\[
A(\nu,d)
=-k_BT\log\int
 \delta\!\left(\nu^T(q-c)-d\right)
 e^{-V(q)/(k_BT)}\,dq .
\]

Transition-state theory is variational: maximizing \(A\) minimizes the rate
within this family of hyperplanar dividing surfaces.  An unoriented plane
normal is a point of \(\mathrm{Gr}(D,1)\).  When the reactant-to-product sign
is retained it is represented on \(S^{D-1}\); antipodal normals describe the
same geometric plane with opposite side labels.  Thus the outer problem is

\[
\max_{([\nu],d)\in\mathrm{Gr}(D,1)\times\mathbb R} A(\nu,d),
\]

or the oriented sphere equivalent.  At \(\nu\), a normal update \(w\) is
projected by \(P_\nu=I-\nu\nu^T\), and the retraction is
\((\nu+w)/\|\nu+w\|\).  Held translations, rotations, or user directions
replace the sphere by rgmin's `SubspaceSphere`.  The offset is a Euclidean
factor.  `PlaneOptimizer` assembles those factors as an rgmin
`ProductManifold` and minimizes \(-A\) with its Riemannian trust region.
In ambient dimension \(D=3N\), a unit normal on \(S^{D-1}\) has \(D-1=3N-1\)
degrees of freedom and the signed offset has one, so the combined family has
\(D\) degrees of freedom before held rigid modes. `PlaneOptimizer` optimizes
all \(D-1\) orientational ones. Johannesson and Jonsson (2001) describe the
orientational optimization as \(D-2\) dimensional, as a size comparison with
the one-dimensional translation along the reaction coordinate; they do not
say which direction that count leaves out.

Sample sizing and convergence are separate.  The gradient norm test may grow
the constrained ensemble up to `max_records`.  It does not decide
convergence: the accepted translation and orientation steps must instead be
smaller than `confidence` times their gradient errors propagated through the
current model curvature, or smaller than `tolerance`, for `patience`
consecutive accepted steps.  `max_iterations` and `max_evaluations` return a
finite last estimate with `PlaneOptimizerStatus::MaxIterations` or
`PlaneOptimizerStatus::MaxEvaluations`; sampling noise cannot make the run
unbounded.

Sampling gives the ambient derivatives

\[
{\partial A\over\partial p}
 =\langle\nu^T\nabla V\rangle\nu,\qquad
{\partial A\over\partial\nu}
 =-\left\langle(\nu^T\nabla V)(q-p)\right\rangle ,
\]

followed by tangent projection.  Moving the pivot inside the plane is a
gauge.  Recentering it at the sample centroid leaves the plane unchanged
and expresses the rotational derivative as the corresponding covariance.

The `ohtst` Cargo feature is opt-in.  There is one shared `Hyperplane` type;
`Hyperplane::new` stores a unit normal and `Hyperplane::from_path` retains
PAFI's path derivative only to preserve the historical \(nn^T/(n^Tn)\)
operation order.  The analytic two-dimensional unit test uses
\(V(x,y)=-x^2/2+y^2\), whose constrained Gaussian has its closed-form
optimal plane at \(x=0\), normal to the unstable mode.

### Twisted-path PAFI and OH-TST observables

For Bligaard and Jónsson's
\[
V(x,y)={V_0\over\cosh^2(\alpha x/2)}
       +{1\over2}\mu\omega^2(y-Cx)^2 ,
\]
the checked analytic reference integrates each line through the saddle only
to the stated \(V_0+22k_BT\) energy cutoff.  It scans the line orientation
and compares free energies relative to the paper's reference orientation.
The same test then exercises the rotation-only `PlaneOptimizer` through
`AnalyticSurfaceSampler` and `HyperplaneSampler`.

At \(T=0.01E_a/k_B\), the cutoff quadrature gives a low-angle maximum of
\(1.16954^\circ\); the paper quotes \(1.24^\circ\).  The test records that
measured discrepancy and does not weaken quadrature or manufacture the
published number.

PAFI and OH-TST answer different questions on this surface.  PAFI fixes a
reaction path \(X(s)\), samples planes normal to that path, estimates
\(dF/ds\), and integrates a one-dimensional potential of mean force.  It
does not rotate those planes.  OH-TST instead holds a candidate dividing
line through the saddle and varies its orientation to maximize its
constrained free energy.  The abrupt low-angle/high-angle branch switch is
therefore an OH-TST variational result; PAFI sees it only if a separately
chosen path supplies the corresponding family of plane normals.

## The constrained ensemble belongs to an MD engine

rgsaddle owns plane geometry and statistical estimators, not production
molecular dynamics.  `HyperplaneSampler` is the engine boundary.  Its input
is a `HyperplaneSampleBudget` containing \(k_BT\), seed, equilibration,
stride, record count, position-retention request, and an explicit coordinate
convention.  `MassWeighted` means \(q=M^{1/2}x\), with a Euclidean unit
normal.  `Cartesian` means the engine applies its configured masses when it
projects momenta and forces.

Each `HyperplaneObservation` reports the mechanical constraint force
\(-\nu^T\nabla V\), an optional complete PAFI gradient record, the PAFI
Jacobian term \(\psi\), an optional position, the force after constrained
directions have been removed, and any velocity component removed by the
integrator.  A general engine need only return positions and the unit-normal
constraint force for PAFI: rgsaddle derives \(\psi\) and the path-normal
scaling from the path geometry.  The complete PAFI record is used by the
analytic reference backend to retain its historical floating-point operation
order.  `HyperplaneEnsemble` adds engine force-call accounting and an
acceptance fraction.  PAFI and OH-TST consume these records; they compute
means, torques, Jacobian corrections, autocorrelation times, block errors,
and retained configurations without knowing the engine handle type.

`AnalyticSurfaceSampler<S: PointSurface>` is the named reference backend.
It keeps the existing projected BAOAB/GHMC dynamics for analytic-surface
tests only.  PAFI's historical overdamped analytic sampler also implements
the interface so its seeded bit dump remains unchanged.  Neither is the
production path.

### Restricted MD, curvature, and thermodynamic integration

Restricted molecular dynamics and proton-transfer thermodynamic integration
use the same boundary rather than a second constrained eigensolver or Gaussian
sampler.

For a plane with additional orthonormal constrained rows \(U\), define
\[
Q=I-\nu\nu^T-U^TU,\qquad H_{\cal H}v=QH(Qv).
\]
The implemented API is

```rust
Hyperplane::hessian_vector(
    surface: &impl PointSurface,
    vector: ArrayView1<f64>,
    constrained_rows: ArrayView2<f64>,
    config: &MinModeConfig,
) -> Result<Array1<f64>, SaddleError>;

Hyperplane::lowest_modes(
    surface: &impl PointSurface,
    constrained_rows: ArrayView2<f64>,
    count: usize,
    config: &MinModeConfig,
    ) -> Result<HyperplaneModes, SaddleError>;
```

Both calls are thin public entries to rgsaddle's existing
`PointSurface::hessian_vector` / finite-difference action and block-Lanczos
implementation.  They must project the trial vector before the action and
the result afterwards.  `HyperplaneModes` reports the shared workspace's
Hessian-action and finite-difference evaluation counts.  The analytic test
checks the restricted Ritz values and vectors against the exact projected
Hessian.

An `ExactGaussianPlaneSampler` implements `HyperplaneSampler` for a
quadratic model \(V(q)=V_c+g^T(q-c)+\tfrac12(q-c)^TH(q-c)\).  It obtains the
positive in-plane spectrum from `Hyperplane::lowest_modes`, draws independent
normal coordinates with variance \(k_BT/\lambda_i\), and reports the same
positions, normal constraint forces, projected forces, and Jacobian fields
as an MD engine.  Zero or negative free curvatures are typed model errors.

Thermodynamic integration uses
\[
V_\lambda=(1-\lambda)V_{\rm harmonic}+\lambda V_{\rm full},\qquad
{dF\over d\lambda}
=\left\langle V_{\rm full}-V_{\rm harmonic}\right\rangle_{\lambda,{\cal H}} .
\]
The sampler request has an extensible observable selector and each returned
record has named scalar observables.  The implemented estimator API is:

```rust
trait HyperplaneSampler {
    fn sample_hyperplane(
        &mut self,
        plane: &Hyperplane,
        budget: &HyperplaneSampleBudget,
    ) -> Result<HyperplaneEnsemble, SaddleError>;
}

fn thermodynamic_integration<E: HyperplaneSampler>(
    sampler: &mut E,
    plane: &Hyperplane,
    config: &ThermodynamicIntegrationConfig,
) -> Result<ThermodynamicIntegrationEstimate, SaddleError>;
```

The TI estimator selects Gauss-Legendre nodes, consumes the named
\(V_{\rm full}-V_{\rm harmonic}\) series, applies the same automated
equilibration and `block_mean` implementation as PAFI and OH-TST, and uses
independent per-node block errors.  Backend-specific Hamiltonian
interpolation remains behind the sampler.  The
`restricted_thermodynamic_integration` spelling documents the Amsel-style
fixed-plane MD/TI use: it does not optimize or move the chosen plane.

### Complete OH-TST workflow on engine traits

Amsel's Cu run demonstrates why a sampled plane factor must not be labelled
OH-TST by itself.  The complete path has three first-class operations:

```rust
optimize_plane(&mut impl HyperplaneSampler, initial, config)
    -> Result<PlaneOptimum, SaddleError>;
reversible_work(&mut impl HyperplaneSampler, path, config)
    -> Result<WorkEstimate, SaddleError>;
transmission_coefficient(&mut impl HyperplaneDynamics, plane, config)
    -> Result<TransmissionCoefficient, SaddleError>;
```

`optimize_plane` and `reversible_work` use repeated constrained ensembles and
depend only on `HyperplaneSampler`.  BAR and MBAR request optional arbitrary
configuration energies through the same engine trait.  The transmission coefficient
\(\kappa\) does not: it launches flux-weighted configurations from the plane
and propagates unconstrained trajectories to basin commitment.  A separate
`HyperplaneDynamics` engine trait exposes that shooting operation.
`AnalyticSurfaceDynamics` is the BAOAB/Newtonian analytic reference.
Pretending that `sample_hyperplane` can provide those operations would hide
the recrossing correction.  `ohtst_rate` combines the free-energy factor and
\(\kappa\) only when both typed results are present.

### Derived equilibration and drift rejection

`thermalize` (PAFI) and `burn_in` (OH-TST) are minimum engine warm-up floors,
not declarations that equilibrium has been reached.  After that floor the
estimator applies John D. Chodera, /A Simple Method for Automated
Equilibration Detection in Molecular Simulations/, /Journal of Chemical
Theory and Computation/ 12, 1799-1805 (2016),
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.5b00784.  For every candidate discard \(t_0\), it
estimates the statistical inefficiency

\[
g(t_0)=\max(1,2\tau(t_0))
\]

and selects the tail maximizing

\[
N_{\mathrm{eff}}(t_0)={N-t_0\over g(t_0)}.
\]

The candidate scan is coarse-to-fine for bounded cost, followed by an exact
scan around the best coarse candidate.  PAFI applies it to the plane-gradient
series; OH-TST applies it to the constraint-force series.  Statistics are
then computed only from the selected tail.

A second, independent stationarity guard splits that tail in half.  It
requires

\[
\left|\bar f_1-\bar f_2\right|\le 4\sqrt{\mathrm{SE}_1^2+\mathrm{SE}_2^2},
\]

where each standard error comes from correlation-length block means.  The
factor four is a conservative four-sigma guard: it rejects visible drift
without treating an ordinary finite-sample fluctuation as failed
equilibration; a 32-ulp scale floor handles analytically constant series.
`EquilibrationReport` records the floor plus selected
discard, \(\tau\), \(N_{\mathrm{eff}}\), drift, error, threshold, and
pass/fail.  A failed guard returns `SaddleError::NotEquilibrated`; no plane
estimate is silently emitted.

### Production backends

- *LAMMPS through OmniPotentRPC/lammpc.* `LammpsHyperplaneSampler` loads the
  pinned rgpot potential profile and creates a lammpc session. lammpc's
  projected BAOAB stepper constrains \(\nu^T(q-p)=0\), projects force and
  velocity in the selected coordinate convention, thermostats tangent
  velocity, and restores the plane after each drift. It returns the scalar
  constraint force, removed velocity, position, projected force, and force
  call count. Hard-region enforcement remains pending the constrained-step
  callback capability described above. No LAMMPS class or pointer appears in
  the Rust trait.
- *OpenMM.*  The adapter may represent the signed plane coordinate with a
  `CustomCVForce` plus a constraint-force readback, or use a
  constraint-projection integrator.  It must expose the same scalar
  constraint force, projected velocity, positions, mass/unit convention,
  step budget, and seed mapping.  A penalty restraint without exact
  constraint-force recovery is not equivalent.
- *GROMACS.*  The adapter uses pull code configured for a plane coordinate,
  reached through the supported API.  It must return the pull constraint
  force, removed momentum or the Jacobian term, optional positions, units,
  masses, step/evaluation accounting, and seed mapping.  Text-log scraping
  is not an API.

The C ABI is callback based so the engine retains ownership:

```c
typedef struct rgsaddle_hyperplane_sampler rgsaddle_hyperplane_sampler;
typedef struct rgsaddle_hyperplane_budget rgsaddle_hyperplane_budget;
typedef struct rgsaddle_hyperplane_observation rgsaddle_hyperplane_observation;

typedef int32_t (*rgsaddle_sample_hyperplane_fn)(
    void *engine_context,
    const double *point,
    const double *unit_normal,
    size_t dimension,
    const rgsaddle_hyperplane_budget *budget,
    int32_t (*emit)(void *, const rgsaddle_hyperplane_observation *),
    void *emit_context);

int32_t rgsaddle_hyperplane_thermodynamic_integration(
    rgsaddle_hyperplane_sampler *, /* plane, config, output */);
```

The opaque sampler stores the callback, engine context, coordinate
convention, units, and masses.  The observation uses borrowed arrays valid
only during `emit`.  Construction, destruction, fixed-layout budget and
observation structs, and fixed-plane TI are implemented at ABI minor 42.
The Python binding presents the same operation as
`hyperplane_thermodynamic_integration` and calls a Python-owned sampler at
every Gauss-Legendre node.
The callback receives the plane point and normal, the coupling lambda, the
thermal energy, the seed, and the thermalize, stride, and sample counts, and
returns float64 C-contiguous observations of `V_full - V_harmonic`.
Callback bindings for plane optimization,
reversible work, PAFI profiles, and unconstrained shooting remain designed
but not implemented.

## Dimer, Lanczos, bands, and Sella are one operator family

For a unit direction \(u\), define

\[
P_u=I-uu^T,\qquad H_u=I-2uu^T=2P_u-I .
\]

`P_u` keeps the perpendicular component and `H_u` reflects the parallel
component.  NEB uses \(P_tF\) for the true force and the complementary
rank-one part for its spring force.  A climbing image uses \(H_tF\).
Dimer translation and Lanczos min-mode following use \(H_uF\) after their
different procedures have supplied \(u\).  The projection is identical;
only the source and update of the direction differ.

Sella equalities \(c(x)=0\) have Jacobian \(J\).  Their tangent projector is

\[
P_J=I-J^T(JJ^T)^+J .
\]

For one normalized row \(J=\nu^T\), \(P_J=P_\nu\).  Sella's
internal-coordinate constraints, a PAFI plane, an OH-TST plane, NEB
nudging, and min-mode force splitting are therefore rank-\(k\) members of
the same projector family.  Nonlinear Sella constraints differ only because
\(J(x)\) and the restoration retraction must be recomputed at each point.

The first shared code piece is deliberately small:

- `TangentProjector` owns force/vector projection.
- `ProjectedConstraint` adds level-set restoration.
- `Hyperplane` is shared by PAFI and OH-TST and retains PAFI's raw path
  derivative only for bitwise-stable projection.
- `HyperplaneSampler` is the engine-neutral constrained-ensemble boundary.
- `UnitNormal` retains the historical band/dimer/Lanczos arithmetic.
- `ManifoldTangent` binds any rgmin `Manifold`, including Sella's
  `Constraints`, at a point.
- PAFI, OH-TST, and `stencil::perp` use these shared implementations.

The checked-in before/after bit dump covers a seeded PAFI sample and the
unit-normal projector.  It is in addition to the existing PAFI, band,
min-mode, Sella, and rgmin manifold tests.

## Reproducing the OH-TST paper is a separate validation piece

The present change validates the implementation; it does not claim to
reproduce published numbers.  A reproduction of Jóhannesson and Jónsson requires all of the
following to be pinned in a separate validation directory:

1. the paper's Appendix-B potential and derivatives, parameters, reduced
   units, masses, and every reported temperature;
2. the initial saddle plane and the allowed position/orientation degrees of
   freedom for each model;
3. a converged line integral or constrained-sampling protocol for every
   trial plane, including domain truncation, quadrature tolerance or
   thermostat, friction, time step, equilibration, stride, and sample count;
4. the outer-plane stopping rule and the handling of the \(\nu\sim-\nu\)
   gauge;
5. reactant partition-function boundaries and the flux prefactor used to
   convert the optimized plane free energy to the OH-TST rate;
6. the dynamical transmission-coefficient definition, launch distribution,
   basin commitment rule, trajectory length, and recrossing convention when
   comparing corrected rates;
7. deterministic seeds plus raw per-plane force, torque, uncertainty, free
   energy, and rate outputs;
8. digitized paper tables/figures with provenance, units, and an explicit
   numerical acceptance tolerance chosen before the comparison.

Without those inputs, agreement with a plotted or rounded paper value is not
a reproducible test.

## Ranked remaining unification pieces

1. *Rank-\(k\) metric projector.* Move Sella's row-space orthogonalisation,
   held-mode projection, and OH-TST subspace projection behind one
   rank-revealing \(J\)-projector with Euclidean and diagonal-mass metrics.
   This removes the largest remaining duplication and must preserve the
   present rank threshold and operation order.
2. *Point-dependent constraint adapter.* Add a fallible constraint API that
   returns \(J(x)\), projects tangents, and restores a trial point.  Migrate
   Sella `Constraints` and then expose it as an rgmin manifold without
   swallowing shape or restoration errors.
3. *Shared Householder functions.* Express climbing image, dimer translation,
   Lanczos translation, and band perpendicular splitting through paired
   `project`/`reflect` functions while retaining each call site's current
   arithmetic and golden hashes.
4. *Mass metric as an explicit type.* Replace repeated square-root mass
   vectors in PAFI/OH-TST/IRC with a checked metric object that maps points,
   tangent vectors, and covectors distinctly.
5. *Additional production engine adapters.* Implement OpenMM and GROMACS
   against `HyperplaneSampler` and the C ABI contract above.
6. *Production callback bindings.* Complete callback-owned C and Python
   engine adapters for optimization, work, TI, and shooting without exposing
   an engine pointer to Rust.
7. *Paper reproduction suite.* Implement the eight pinned inputs above and
   compare paper observables only after independent quadrature references
   pass.

# Crystal operations and symmetry-unique regions (`docs/orgmode/explanation/symmetry-regions.org`)

> Crystal symmetry operations, path multiplicity, and hard Voronoi regions

## Construction

A host supplies three-dimensional orthogonal matrices, optional affine
translations or rotation centres, and reactant and saddle Cartesian
geometries.  An operation acts on an atom at \(x\) as

\[
x' = R(x-c)+c+t.
\]

The operation may also carry a source-to-target atom permutation.  When it
does not, rgsaddle matches transformed reactant atoms to reactant atoms of
the same species.  Periodic distances and the final unwrapping use
`minimage::Cell::displacement_euclidean`.  The implementation does not
duplicate a minimum-image convention.

This is a consumer API, not a space-group finder.  The host remains
responsible for supplying the candidate crystallographic operations.
The affine form and the distinction between point and space-group
operations follow the conventions in International Tables for
Crystallography, Volume A, edited by Theo Hahn, 5th edition (2005),
doi:10.1107/97809553602060000100.

## Path multiplicity and region degeneracy

Operations which map the reactant onto itself form the reactant stabilizer
\(H\).  Applied to the selected saddle, they produce an orbit.  The path
multiplicity is the number of distinct images

\[
m_{\rm path} ` |H \cdot s| ` {|H| \over |H_s|},
\]

where \(H_s\) is the joint stabilizer, the subgroup of \(H\) that also maps
that saddle to itself.  This is the orbit-stabilizer theorem; see
Jean-Pierre Serre, /Linear Representations of Finite Groups/, Springer
(1977), doi:10.1007/978-1-4684-9458-7.  \(m_{\rm path}\) is the number of
equivalent hops.  Callers pass it to `RateMultiplicity::with_paths`.  It is
not the degeneracy of the sampled cell.

\(H_s\) is the symmetry of one hop.  Each of its operations fixes the
reactant and the saddle, and therefore maps the dividing plane of that hop
onto itself.  The region degeneracy is the order \(|H_s|\).  The returned
`SymmetryUniqueRegion` is the asymmetric unit of that plane, the Dirichlet
cell of one generic in-plane point under \(H_s\), and `Region::degeneracy`
reports the same order.  Faces lie in the plane.  Sampling the cell and
multiplying by \(|H_s|\) restores the full plane of that one hop.
Multiplying again by \(m_{\rm path}\) counts the other hops.

Jóhannesson and Jónsson, /Optimization of hyperplanar transition states/,
/The Journal of Chemical Physics/ 115, 9644-9656 (2001),
doi:10.1063/1.1415499, build this kind of restricted sample in Sec. II D
("Incorporation of symmetry").  For an \(n\)-fold axis, half-lines start at
the reactant minimum and run toward each symmetry-equivalent product.  The
sample is kept in the sector of one product: a step that comes closer to
another half-line is rejected and the velocity is reflected in the mirror
that exchanges the two product directions.  Their Eqs. 13-17 remove the
part of that mirror normal parallel to the hyperplane normal, so the
reflection stays in the plane.  Sec. III D ("Al adatom diffusion on
Al(100)") uses the fourfold form of this construction for every thermal
sample.  Without the constraint, the optimized hyperplane was an average of
two symmetrically equivalent concerted-displacement channels.

An identity-only group has path multiplicity one, region degeneracy one,
and no faces.  The full octahedral stabilizer of an fcc vacancy sends one
nearest-neighbour hop to twelve images.  Those twelve are the path
multiplicity.  The region degeneracy is \(|H_s|\) for that hop, the
operations that fix both the vacancy reactant and the chosen saddle.

## Validation and tolerances

The constructor rejects non-finite data, non-orthogonal matrices,
non-bijective permutations, and permutations that map unlike species.
Operations that are valid group operations but do not stabilize the
particular reactant are omitted from \(H\).  Matching, orbit, and
orthogonality tolerances are explicit fields of
`CrystalSymmetryConfig`.  Callers should choose them for their coordinate
units and structure accuracy instead of relying on a hidden physical
tolerance.

For periodic cells the nearest-image displacement is the standard
simulation-cell convention described by Daan Frenkel and Berend Smit,
/Understanding Molecular Simulation/, 2nd edition, Academic Press (2002),
doi:10.1016/B978-0-12-267351-1.X5000-7.

# Architecture (`docs/orgmode/reference/architecture.org`)

> Crate architecture and module boundaries

The host supplies the potential surface and owns the outer search loop. rgsaddle supplies band force assembly, minimum-mode rotation, restricted index-1 steps, Sella sessions, intrinsic reaction coordinate integration and molecular dynamics mechanics.

Band and minimum-mode translation use rgmin's solver. Dense quadratic restriction is available through `rgsaddle::trust`, which re-exports rgmin's dense controller. The root `rgsaddle::TrustRegion` accepts a spectrum for Sella steps. The projected band trust method is implemented by `BandRtr`.

`PointSurface` accepts one coordinate vector. `BandSurface` accepts a collection of images. The C callback expresses either request with the same official structure. The library has no Message Passing Interface (MPI) dependency; a host can evaluate a request collectively or distribute image work itself.

Hessian storage and updates live in `pes` and `qn`. `linalg` supplies numerical actions and cached direction/action pairs. `eigensolve` supplies dense and iterative eigenproblems. `sparse_hessian` builds a cutoff Hessian by a direct Curtis-Powell-Reid partition of a distance-2 colouring and implements `ApplyHessian`. Molecular topology enters through `vocn` and the equality chart. Periodic differences use linkcell.

# LAMMPS hyperplane API (`docs/orgmode/reference/lammps-hyperplane.org`)

> LAMMPS hyperplane sampler contract and C ABI hooks

## Cargo feature

`lammps` is opt-in and enables `ohtst`. It adds the pinned
`rgpot-core` profile dependency. `liblammpc` and `liblammps` are runtime
shared libraries and are not needed by default builds.

## Public types

| Type | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `LammpsSystem` | Flat `PotentialConfig`, Cartesian positions, atomic numbers, masses, and optional cell |
| `LammpsSamplerConfig` | Shared library path, BAOAB time step in ps, Langevin friction in inverse ps, thermostat kind, the excluded-mode count used in \(3N - 1 - n_{\mathrm{excluded}}\), and an optional Taylor reference for lambda mixing |
| `LammpsThermodynamicReference` | Reference geometry, energy, gradient, and dense Hessian in the sampler coordinates of the plane |
| `LammpsThermostatKind` | Thermostat enum stored in records; currently `BaoabLangevin` |
| `LammpsThermostatRecord` | Serializable thermostat metadata with `thermostat` and `effective_degrees_of_freedom` |
| `LammpsHyperplaneSampler` | Persistent lammpc session implementing `HyperplaneSampler` |

All configuration structs are `#[non_exhaustive]`, implement `Default`, and
provide `with_*` builders. A default system is incomplete and validation
returns `SaddleError::Invalid` or `SaddleError::Shape` before loading the
engine.

## Units and coordinates

The rgpot `ForceInput` uses angstrom and eV. LAMMPS uses `metal` units.
The sampler controls use:

| Quantity | Unit |
| --- | --- |
| time step | ps |
| friction | ps^-1 |
| thermal energy | eV |
| mass | amu |

`HyperplaneCoordinates::MassWeighted` passes the plane in
\(q=M^{1/2}x\). Returned positions are \(q\), forces are
\(F_q=M^{-1/2}F_x\), and velocities are \(\dot q=M^{1/2}\dot x\).

`HyperplaneCoordinates::Cartesian` passes Cartesian point and normal. lammpc
uses the diagonal mass metric when restoring positions and projecting
velocity and force.

## Thermostat metadata and records

Each `HyperplaneObservation` from `LammpsHyperplaneSampler` carries two stable
scalar observables:

| Observable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lammps.thermostat` | Numeric code of `LammpsThermostatKind` (1 for `BaoabLangevin`) |
| `lammps.effective_degrees_of_freedom` | \(3N - 1 - n_{\mathrm{excluded}}\) |

`LammpsThermostatRecord::to_json` writes
`rgsaddle.lammps_thermostat` documents, and `from_json` reads the same
format.

## lammpc constrained MD extension

The adapter requires these additive C ABI functions:

```c
int lammpc_session_md_initialize(...);
int lammpc_session_md_step(LammpcSession *, size_t);
int lammpc_session_md_state(...);
```

`md_initialize` receives one rgpot `ForceInput`, a point, a normal, and
`LammpcMdConfig`. `md_step` advances exactly the requested number of BAOAB
steps. `md_state` returns positions, projected forces, removed velocities,
the scalar constraint force, the force-evaluation count, and the completed
step count.

LAMMPS hard-region sampling additionally requires lammpc to advertise that
`md_step` applies a registered hard-boundary callback, restores the complete
accepted state on rejection, and refreshes projected forces after reflection.
The callback registration symbols alone do not establish this behavior.
Current lammpc main does not provide it, so the adapter fails closed for a
sampling budget with a region.

The extension is generic. It does not contain an OH-TST, PAFI, pair-style,
or material type. rgsaddle maps those arrays into `HyperplaneObservation`.

## Thermodynamic integration coupling

When `HyperplaneSampleBudget::lambda` is set, `LammpsHyperplaneSampler`
requires `LammpsSamplerConfig::thermodynamic_reference`: a Taylor harmonic
model stored as reference geometry, energy, gradient, and dense Hessian in
the sampler coordinates of the plane. Those are the coordinates selected by
`HyperplaneSampleBudget::coordinates` and passed to `md_initialize`.

Until lammpc exposes a mixing hook, lambda sampling fails with a surface
error. The additive ABI is:

```c
typedef struct {
  double lambda;
  double reference_energy;
} lammpc_md_thermodynamic_coupling_t;

int lammpc_session_md_set_thermodynamic_coupling(
    LammpcSession *session,
    const lammpc_md_thermodynamic_coupling_t *coupling,
    const double *reference_point,
    const double *reference_gradient,
    const double *reference_hessian,
    size_t dimension);
```

`reference_point`, `reference_gradient`, and `reference_hessian` are in the
sampler frame. The Hessian is passed already symmetrized. Each MD step adds
`(1-lambda) F_harmonic` in that frame, with
`F_harmonic ` -(g_0 + H (x - x_0))=, and the engine converts that force to
the Cartesian LAMMPS force with the same mass metric it uses for the
constraint. The hook is not tied to a pair style or a material.

The observable also needs the unmixed full potential. A missing symbol is a
surface error when lambda is set:

```c
int lammpc_session_md_potential_energy(
    LammpcSession *session,
    const double *position,
    size_t dimension,
    double *energy);
```

`position` is the Cartesian geometry returned by `md_state`. The scalar
energy is frame invariant. rgsaddle evaluates `V_harm` itself at the
sampler-frame image of that geometry, including the mass-weighted scaling
`q ` M^{1/2} x= when the budget asks for mass-weighted coordinates.

## Errors

Library lookup follows rgpot's `lammpc` profile candidates. An explicit path
has priority, followed by `LAMMPC_LIBRARY`, `RGPOT_LAMMPC_ENGINE`, and
platform library names. Missing symbols, an unavailable stub build, ABI
mismatch, invalid geometry, and LAMMPS failures become
`SaddleError::Surface` with lammpc's diagnostic.

The sentence is the comment above the declaration.
Parameters are that declaration.
Units are the caller's unless the sentence names them.
The narrative for a session is the C and C++ how-to, not this list.

- `rgsaddle_minmode_set_saddle_check`. Purpose: rgsaddle_band_set_saddle_check for a min-mode session. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_minmode_saddle_index`. Purpose: rgsaddle_band_saddle_index for a min-mode session. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_ocineb_set_saddle_check`. Purpose: rgsaddle_band_set_saddle_check for an OCI-NEB session. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_ocineb_saddle_index`. Purpose: rgsaddle_band_saddle_index for an OCI-NEB session. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_saddle_index`. Purpose: Certify one point, ABI minor 40. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_config_default`. Purpose: Fill out with the default growing-string controls (n_images 11, frontier_tol 0.2, min_steps_per_node 1, not-a-knot spline), ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_create`. Purpose: Open a growing string session between reactant and product (3 * n_atoms values each), ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_step`. Purpose: Advance a growing string session by one step (or one simplified-string step once joined), ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_n_images`. Purpose: Active image count of a growing string session (left_nodes + right_nodes while growing, n_images once joined), or 0 for NULL, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_nodes_added`. Purpose: Nodes the last rgsaddle_growing_string_step grew on the reactant and product fragments (0, 1, or 2), or 0 for NULL and before the first step, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_phase`. Purpose: Phase of a growing string session (RGSADDLE_GROWING_STRING_GROWING or RGSADDLE_GROWING_STRING_JOINED), or RGSADDLE_NULL_SESSION for NULL, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_positions`. Purpose: Copy the active positions (rgsaddle_growing_string_n_images(session) * 3 * n_atoms values) into out, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_ids`. Purpose: Copy the stable image identifiers (rgsaddle_growing_string_n_images(session) uint64_t values) into out, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_set_fixed_atoms`. Purpose: Replace the per-atom fixed mask (n_atoms bytes, 1 fixed and 0 free) on a growing string session, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_saddle_index`. Purpose: Read the saddle-index certificate of a joined growing string session, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_growing_string_free`. Purpose: Free a growing string session, ABI minor 44. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_band_set_free_end`. Purpose: Enable, replace, or clear the free-end adaptive NEB (FEA-NEB) of Zhang, Zhang, Ye, and Zheng, J. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_band_free_end_residual`. Purpose: Read the signed target-energy residual `E(x_end) - E_target` from the most recent free-end step into `out`, ABI minor 45. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.
- `rgsaddle_band_free_end_cuts`. Purpose: Number of adaptive cut-and-remesh refinements performed so far on a free-end band, or 0 for NULL, ABI minor 45. Parameters: the declaration. Units: the caller's.

# Contributing (`docs/orgmode/contributing/index.org`)

> Build, test, MSRV, Python stub, documentation, and release workflow

## System prerequisites
- The current stable Rust with clippy and rustfmt; CI formats, lints and tests with it.
- rustup and jq, which the minimum supported Rust version checks below use to install the toolchain that `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` names.
- A C compiler, and a C++ compiler with C++17 support and its standard library headers.
  The C and C++ smoke tests call `cc` and `c++`, or the compilers named by `CC` and `CXX`.
  The CMake builds below use the same compilers.
  If Clang cannot find `cstddef`, set `CXX=g++`.
  Or install the libstdc++ development package for the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC) version that Clang selects.
- GNU m4, which the GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) build behind the `verify` feature needs.
  On Debian and Ubuntu install the `m4` package.
- CMake, which the `chemfiles` and `highs` features use to build native libraries.
  CMake 4 needs `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for the chemfiles build.
  [Read a molecular frame](/howto/io.html) uses the same setting.

## Build and test
Build and test a pinned checkout with its Cargo lockfile.
The C and C++ smoke tests require the C ABI library as well as the test executables.

```sh
cargo build --locked --features capi
cargo test --locked --features capi
CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

Optional features are checked with their dependencies enabled.
The `faer` feature is part of the default set.
It is the dense self-adjoint spectrum used by connect and SQNM.
The Kani workflow's prove step builds with `--no-default-features --features capi` so that job does not compile `pulp`.
The `kani-github-action` default command is a bare `cargo-kani`, which would enable `faer`.
The workflow overrides that command and does not pass `--ignore-global-asm`.
Build the Python package with scikit-build-core (`pip install .`) and run `tests/python` against the installed package.
The algebra and interval checks live in `validation` and `tests/symbolic`; the Lean libraries live in `formal`.
The verify workflow's symbolic-script step runs those checks and leaves `validation/benchmark/` out.
Those files are the pt-island campaign drivers.
They import optbench and take a checkout plus a long run, so they are not part of the minute-long symbolic check.

A git dependency names a full 40-character `rev`, never a `tag` or `branch`, with the exact version of the crate at that commit, such as `version = "=0.5.2"`.
Cargo keys a git source by its reference, so a dependent that pins the same commit another way locks a second copy.
`ci/consumer` is such a dependent: it takes this checkout by path and pins linkcell, rgmin and rgpot-core by rev.
Bump its revs together with `Cargo.toml`.
The CI test job runs the check and compiles the consumer:

```sh
python3 ci/check_dependency_pins.py
cargo check --manifest-path ci/consumer/Cargo.toml --target-dir target
```

## Minimum supported Rust version
The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is the `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`.
A change must not need a newer compiler, and must pass the MSRV checks below as well as the stable ones.
Clippy adds and revises lints between releases, so code that stable's clippy accepts can fail the MSRV's, and the reverse.
The `msrv` job of the CI workflow reads `rust-version` with `cargo metadata` and installs that toolchain.
It runs the clippy steps of the test and readcon jobs and of the verify workflow's rust job on it, then builds and tests `--features capi`, all with `--locked`.
A dependency in `Cargo.lock` that needs a newer compiler fails the job.
Edition 2024's resolver avoids that when it can: `cargo update` prefers versions that support the MSRV.
To raise the MSRV, edit `rust-version`; the job and the commands below read it from there.
These commands reproduce the job:

```sh
msrv=$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq -er '.packages[] | select(.name == "rgsaddle") | .rust_version')
rustup toolchain install "$msrv" --profile minimal --component clippy
cargo +"$msrv" clippy --locked --features capi -- -D warnings
cargo +"$msrv" clippy --locked --all-targets --features readcon -- -D warnings
cargo +"$msrv" clippy --locked --all-targets --features readcon,readcon-db -- -D warnings
cargo +"$msrv" clippy --locked --all-targets --features capi,verify -- -D warnings
cargo +"$msrv" build --locked --features capi
cargo +"$msrv" test --locked --features capi
```

## Python stub
`python/rgsaddle/_core.pyi` is the output of nanobind's stubgen on the installed extension.
Do not edit it by hand.
The typing job of the Python binding workflow regenerates it with nanobind 3.1.0 and fails on any difference.
The extension renders its own signatures, so `build-system.requires` in `pyproject.toml` pins the same nanobind.
Give a binding that takes a callable or returns a tuple an `nb::sig`, as `connect` does; a bare `Callable` or `tuple` fails `mypy --strict`.
After a change to `bind/ext.cpp`, rebuild against the pinned nanobind and regenerate the stub:

```sh
python -m pip install 'nanobind==3.1.0' 'scikit-build-core>=1.1'
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation .
python scripts/regen_stub.py
```

`python scripts/regen_stub.py --check` prints the difference and exits nonzero, as the typing job does.
The script reads the pin from `pyproject.toml` and refuses another nanobind.

## Documentation
Narrative pages are the Org sources under `docs/orgmode`.
`docs/export.el` writes a reStructuredText file under `docs/source` for each of them.
Git ignores those files, so edit the Org source and do not add the generated files.
Build the site as the docs workflow does:

```sh
emacs --batch -l docs/export.el
python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
sphinx-build -b html -n docs/source docs/build
```

The API documentation builds with every rustdoc warning denied on each feature set CI tests, and once with private items.
A public doc that links a private item, a broken or redundant intra-doc link, a bare URL or unclosed HTML fails the CI test job.
The crate overview links the optional `ohtst` module only when that feature is enabled.
A default-feature build names the module and the `ohtst` feature in code font, because the module is not compiled.
Each entry point opens with an example on a small analytic surface, which `cargo test` runs.

```sh
ci/check_rustdoc.sh
cargo test --locked --doc --features capi
```

Retain numerical assertions and record the source, dependency and library revisions with performance results.

## Changelog
Each change adds a fragment under `docs/newsfragments`
and leaves `docs/orgmode/changelog.org` as it is.
Name the fragment `+<slug>.<type>.org`, or `<issue>.<type>.org` for a
change with an issue number.
The types are the sections of `towncrier.toml`: `breaking`, `security`,
`removed`, `deprecated`, `added`, `doc`, `dev`, `changed`, `fixed` and `misc`.
Write Org markup with one sentence per line.
A release collects the fragments under a new heading, and `--draft`
prints that heading without writing it:
```sh
python -m pip install towncrier
towncrier build --draft --version <version>
towncrier build --version <version>
```

## Release to PyPI
A `v*` tag publishes the crate to crates.io through `publish.yml` and the Python package to PyPI through `pypi.yml`.
`pypi.yml` uses PyPI trusted publishing, so the repository holds no PyPI token.
Before the first upload, the PyPI account that will own the project adds a pending publisher at https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/ with these values:

- PyPI Project Name: `rgsaddle`
- Owner: `OmniPotentRPC`
- Repository name: `rgsaddle`
- Workflow name: `pypi.yml`
- Environment name: `pypi`

The first upload creates the project and turns the pending publisher into its trusted publisher.
Only the `publish` job runs in the `pypi` environment and holds `id-token: write`, so required reviewers added to that environment in the repository settings hold every upload until one approves it.

To release a version:

1. Set it in `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml` and `meson.build`; `tests/package_version.rs` holds them equal.
2. Collect the fragments with `towncrier build --version <version>` and commit.
3. Push the tag `v<version>` on that commit.

The `versions` job stops the run unless the tag is `v` followed by the version in both `Cargo.toml` and `pyproject.toml`.
The `wheels` job runs cibuildwheel with the `[tool.cibuildwheel]` table of `pyproject.toml` on Linux `x86_64` and `aarch64`, macOS `arm64` and `x86_64`, and Windows `x86_64`, and tests every wheel.
The `smoke` job installs each platform's wheels into a fresh virtual environment under CPython 3.10, 3.14 and 3.14t, and the sdist under 3.12, and imports the package.
`publish` uploads after every other job has passed.

A pushed tag runs the workflows of the tagged commit, so a tag cut before `pypi.yml` existed, such as `v0.5.0`, does not start it.
Once `pypi.yml` is on the default branch, a manual run with the `tag` input builds and publishes such a tag:

```sh
gh workflow run pypi.yml --ref main -f tag=v0.5.0
```

A deployment branch rule on the `pypi` environment must admit `main` for that run.
A manual run without the input builds and smoke-tests the selected branch and uploads nothing.

## Contact
Report bugs, ask questions and propose changes on the issue tracker at https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgsaddle/issues.
The maintainer is Rohit Goswami (rgoswami@ieee.org), the author listed in `Cargo.toml` and `pyproject.toml`.

## Acknowledgments
The nudged elastic band (NEB) force assembly is ported from eOn [eon2901].
The tangents, springs, projections and climbing-image force keep eOn's branch structure.
They come from eOn's `NEBTangent`, `NEBSpringForce` and `NEBForceProjection`.

Other parts follow existing codes.
AutoNEB follows the window and spring rescaling of the AutoNEB in the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE).
The Sella sessions follow the optimizer, constraints and eigensolvers of Sella.
`nichols_step` and the Powell update follow i-PI under the MIT option of its licence.

The crate builds on rgmin for its steppers and on linkcell for cutoff neighbour walks.
ndarray, faer and rayon supply arrays, dense linear algebra and threads.
The optional features read structure files with readcon-core and chemfiles.
readcon-db stores traces and restarts.
The `verify` checks use rug, which binds GMP and the GNU Multiple Precision Floating-Point Reliable (MPFR) library.
The Python package is built with nanobind, scikit-build-core and Corrosion.
Its `rgsaddle.ase` module uses ASE.
